title: Pack protocol
description: Pack protocol v2 — the messages a runtime exchanges with a pack service to run pack code (tool handlers and guardrail checks). One request, one response. Transport (HTTP): `POST /v1/invoke` takes a request and answers 200 with a response; `GET /v1/info` (token) answers `info`; `GET /healthz` (no token) answers 200 while the process is up; `GET /readyz` (no token) answers 200 once every module the index names has loaded and the service isn't draining. Headers: `kindgi-pack-token` (required on `/v1/invoke` and `/v1/info`; `Authorization` is deliberately not used, since platforms like Cloud Run put their own identity token there), `kindgi-timeout-ms` (relative deadline; default 120000), `kindgi-run-id`, `kindgi-request-id`, `kindgi-protocol`, `traceparent` (W3C Trace Context: the run's trace, so a pack service's records can carry its trace id; optional, protocol 2.4.1); the answer to an invoke carries `kindgi-duration-ms` and `kindgi-artifact-version`. Every outcome of running pack code is a response message with status 200 — a validation failure, a throw, an unknown tool, `deadline-exceeded`, `cancelled` (the caller closed the connection). Non-2xx statuses are transport-level only: 401 (bad token), 404, 405, 413 (body over 10 MiB), 415 (not `application/json`), 503 with `Retry-After` (not ready, draining, or at the concurrency cap — the call provably did not run), 500 (the service itself failed). Process contract: a pack service reads `--index`, `--module-root` and `--host` arguments, `KINDGI_PACK_SERVICE_TOKEN`, `PORT` (`0` picks a free port) and `KINDGI_PACK_SERVICE_MAX_CONCURRENCY`; it removes `KINDGI_PACK_SERVICE_TOKEN` from its process environment before it loads pack code, which never sees it; it loads every module before listening and exits 1 with a `{"kind":"boot-failed","problems":[…]}` JSON line on stderr when one fails; once listening it writes `{"kind":"listening","port":N,…}` on stderr; SIGTERM drains in-flight calls (up to 8 s; `/readyz` and new invokes answer 503 meanwhile) and exits 0.

callContext.description: Per-call context a handler receives. Serializable only: a pack service adds its own cancellation (an abort signal, a cancellation token) on top.

runId.description: The kernel run the call belongs to.

projectId.description: The project of the run the call belongs to. Set by the runtime from the run, never from its input or a model's arguments. Absent from an older runtime.

orgId.description: The org of that project, when the project has one. Set by the runtime from the project, never from input. Absent when the project has no org, and from an older runtime.

requestId.description: The individual call — e.g. the model's tool-call id.

env.description: Resolved environment values for the call (open).

settings.description: The settings blocks the calling agent version pins: each block's values, by block id (protocol 2.4.0). Absent when it pins none, and from an older runtime.

toolInvoke.description: Run a tool handler. The pack service validates `input` against the indexed input schema, runs the handler, validates its return value against the indexed output schema.

id.description: Tool id, resolved from the pack service's own index.

version.description: When set, the pack service refuses a different indexed version (`tool-version-mismatch`).

id.description: Check id (the indexed guardrail's `checkId`, else its `id`).

trace.description: The run trace the check evaluates (`RunTrace` in `@kindgi/guardrails`).

output.description: The handler's return value, valid against the tool's output schema.

errorCode.description: Why running pack code didn't produce a result.

issue.description: One validation issue, Ajv-shaped. `keyword` names the failing JSON Schema keyword; it is absent when the failure came from a model's own validation (a Zod refinement, a pydantic validator) rather than a schema keyword. Open: an implementation may add fields.

instancePath.description: JSON Pointer to the failing value (`""` for the root, `/items/0/name`).

schemaPath.description: URI fragment of the failing schema keyword (`#/properties/name/type`).

params.description: Keyword parameters, as Ajv reports them: `required` → `{ missingProperty }`, `additionalProperties` → `{ additionalProperty }`, `type` → `{ type }`, `enum` → `{ allowedValues }`, limits → `{ limit }`, `pattern` → `{ pattern }`, `format` → `{ format }`.

toolId.description: Present when the error is about a tool.

checkId.description: Present when the error is about a check.

cause.description: The serialized throw for `handler-throw` / `handler-import-failed` (`{ name, message, stack }` for an error object).

missingEnv.description: The index's required env names this process lacks (unset or empty), sorted. Empty when none is missing. Under the `strict` env check the service isn't ready while any is listed.
